course.template: Make a talktrack course that takes someone from no knowledge to working knowledge of {subject}, as 3 to 6 parts. Read the code and docs first, then plan one learning goal per part, in dependency order: no part leans on one that comes later. Say the plan in the opening of the first part. Make each part its own finished walkthrough of 1 to 3 minutes of short slides, one point each, that ends with one quiz slide on its goal, and call `finish_walkthrough` on each part when it is complete. Export each part as an MP4 as soon as it is finished and send it to me, in order, with its goal in one line, before you start the next. Make no playlist and send no links.

explain.template:
Make a narrated talktrack walkthrough that explains this so that someone new to it understands it: {source}

First work out what it is. A link, or the path of a PDF, an image or a text file: read it with `read_source`, which gives the text word for word; for a PDF, read the outline first, then the pages you need. Pasted text, notes or an idea: it is all above. Read the whole source before you plan. Then find the one question it answers or the one idea it carries, the three to six ideas that build up to it, in the order they depend on each other, and the terms a newcomer must know.

Explain it, don't summarise it: open with the big idea in one plain sentence, or with the most concrete example of it, then one idea per slide, each with a picture that carries it: a diagram of how the parts connect, a timeline for events, a chart for numbers, `math` for a formula (say what each term means), a short excerpt for code, a worked example for a method, or the source's own image or figure when it shows the point. Narrate each slide in at most about 50 words: the picture carries the detail, and a point that needs more words gets a slide of its own. For an idea or a plan rather than a finished text, explain what it is, the problem it solves, how it would work and what is still open. Keep to what the source says: say so in the narration when you add background it does not give, and never invent quotes, numbers or sources. Name the source, its title with its author or link, on the opening slide. End with one quiz slide on the main point and a closing slide with the takeaways.

Size it to the source: a paragraph, an idea or an image, 1 to 2 minutes; an article or a paper, 2 to 4 minutes. For a source longer than about 20 pages or 10,000 words, make a course instead: 3 to 6 parts, one learning goal each, in dependency order, the plan said in the opening of the first part, each part its own finished walkthrough of 1 to 3 minutes that ends with one quiz slide; call `finish_walkthrough` on each part, export each part as an MP4 as soon as it is finished and send it to me, in order, with its goal in one line, before you start the next; make no playlist and send no links. For a single walkthrough, export it as an MP4 once it is finished and send it to me.
